messages:
elena: Thanks for coming to the all-hands. Leaving this live thread for follow-ups on mission, market positioning, and competitor strategy. I'll check in across the afternoon.

kevin: Quick from enablement  can we get a one-paragraph 'why Redwood' that reps can use in initial outreach for regulated industries?
mira: product ask: are we updating the public-facing language around 'serving-first' to something shorter for marketing? current phrase is a mouthful for non-technical buyers.
owen: engineering: curious if we should point customers to a short SDK snippet showing the same API across hosted/dedicated/private. That was a strong moment in the demo today.
rachael: GTM: any new direction on competitive comparisons? do we produce a 1-pager for SI partners that calls out hyperscaler gaps?
elena: Answers: 1) Regulated outreach one-paragraph for reps: "Redwood Inference provides a single developer API with SLA-backed performance and private deployment options so teams can meet compliance requirements without re-architecting their apps." Keep it benefits-first and under two sentences.
elena: 2) Marketing shorthand: testing variant: "Serve reliably. Ship faster. Control costs." Short, benefit-led, tweakable per audience.
elena: 3) SDK snippet: yes, show this small example for devs: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(endpoint="https://hosted.redwood")
# switch to private by changing endpoint and token, app code unchanged
resp = client.generate("Summarize quarterly goals")
print(resp.text)
```
Use in dev docs and demo decks.
kevin: that paragraph is helpful. For SI partners should we include a small checklist (compliance items, regional options) with the 1-pager?
elena: Yes  include a short partner checklist: supported regions, KMS/HSM options, audit log retention, SOC/ISO attestations. We'll draft it with partnerships.
mira: public-facing 'serving-first' phrasing  i like the marketing shorthand. Can we A/B test 'Serve reliably' vs 'Serving-first economics'?
elena: Yes, run A/B tests in the next campaign. Keep internal enablement language richer; marketing should be concise.
owen: small follow-up on SDK snippet  can we also add a note about feature parity: function/tool-calling, streaming, and embeddings all work across modes? reps loved that point.
elena: Absolutely  add a bullet: "Feature parity: streaming, function/tool calls, embeddings, and model pinning are supported across hosted, dedicated, and private."
rachael: competitors: should reps use named comparisons in outbound? some teams fear alienating prospects with direct name-checking.
elena: Internal decks can include explicit competitor cards. Customer/outbound messaging should remain product- and benefit-focused; if a prospect names a competitor, reps may compare directly. We'll provide suggested scripts.
kevin: hiring/people question: any change to hiring focus given this GTM tilt? reps ask whether we continue to hire infra-heavy roles vs sales/growth.
elena: We're still infra-forward this half (approx 55-60% infra/serving hires) to support Dedicated and Private growth. Sales and solutions will ramp mid-year.
mira: last: any public benchmark plans? open-source reproducible tests?
elena: Publish high-level benchmark summaries and a small reproducible test harness for the community. Keep full internal lab runs private.
ops-bot: Recording + slides uploaded: https://redwood/ah/1905000000 (auto-upload)
kevin: thanks elena  i'll circulate the rep paragraph and partner checklist template to enablement.
rachael: will prep the SI partner one-pager draft and tag partnerships.
owen: will add the SDK snippet + feature parity bullet to the dev docs.
mira: i'll set up the A/B test for the two marketing lines.
elena: Thanks team  i'll post the partner checklist and the small developer-facing perf blurb by EOD. Keep questions here or DM. :raised_hands:
